statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 13 of 100 in the low band, twelve points below the 25-point block threshold, because CME equity index futures remain inside the regular weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to be pathological. Eleven of the twenty-four forward slots sit inside that closure. Stress is 66 in the high band on oil above $100, a 10-year near 4.95 per cent, a Fed decision on Wednesday with a 25 basis point increase largely priced, and an unresolved Hormuz and Red Sea supply picture. The one structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart, published as a narrow danger window running to 03:00 UTC on Monday rather than a broad session-wide state change.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in eleven of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday for the weekend and are scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend record is severe but is carried in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path currently exists to be pathological; the record is also two-sided, with Monday's Salalah meeting on temporary Hormuz shipping lanes set against the vessel strikes and the Yemen exchanges. Third, the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad shutdown, and even the peak conditional Tail of 24 stays one point below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: With CME equity index futures in their regular weekend closure the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX at 15.84, while an Iranian commercial ship was struck near Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz early Sunday with one dead and four wounded, a second vessel was hit late Saturday, and a Houthi projectile wounded two in Saudi Arabia's Jazan region; Tail stays at 13 because there is no live price path to score, and the published risk is concentrated in the 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent from a 29,103.51 previous close, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high. That was a relief session that recovered part of the preceding four-day decline, and it is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent; the pullback followed Iranian state media confirming that Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz. H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year Treasury at 4.56 per cent and the 10-year at 4.95 per cent, and the 10-year note yield index last quoted 4.975 per cent on Friday. Crude above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset signals raise Stress more than Tail.

Weekend record. An Iranian commercial vessel was struck early Sunday off Qeshm Island with one of ten crew killed and four wounded, and Iranian state media quoted the Qeshm governor blaming a hostile actor; the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre separately reported a vessel hit by a projectile in the strait late Saturday, with a fire and a crew evacuation. Saudi Civil Defence reported that a Houthi projectile wounded two people and damaged a mosque in the Jazan region. Set against that, Oman is seeking to convene GCC foreign ministers and Iran in Salalah on Monday on temporary shipping lanes and mine clearing, with attendance not confirmed. The record is therefore severe but genuinely two-sided.

Why Tail stays low. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. No such path can exist while the reference contract is shut, so none of the usual amplifiers, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or the index holding near a session extreme, is observable in this assessment. The unpriced weekend record is real, but it is gap and headline exposure concentrated at a single scheduled instant, and it is published as such.

Where the risk actually sits. The scheduled 22:00 UTC restart is the only structural checkpoint inside the horizon. Conditional Tail peaks there at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, because the first quotes must absorb the whole weekend record simultaneously in thin liquidity. It then decays through the Asian session on the assumption of orderly two-sided price discovery. Monday's Salalah meeting reaches index risk through the crude channel rather than directly.

Week ahead. No U.S. macro release falls inside this 24-hour horizon. The week's weight sits on Wednesday: August Retail Sales at 12:30 UTC, then the FOMC decision with projections at 18:00 UTC and the press conference at 18:30 UTC, with fed funds pricing implying roughly 85 per cent for a 25 basis point increase to 3.75 to 4.00 per cent as of 12 September. Those are checkpoints for later assessments, not grounds to lift Tail today.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 11:00 UTC on 12 September to 10:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday. Tail held at 6 for the first eighteen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00, 11 at 09:00 and 12 at 10:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow U: it eased from 55 to 50 between 11:00 and 17:00 UTC on 12 September as Friday's relief close and the crude pullback were absorbed, then rebuilt to 66 by 10:00 UTC on 13 September as the weekend Hormuz and Yemen record accumulated. Confidence stayed between 85 and 87 throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green in normal mode, so no lookback hour reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: Eleven of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's twelfth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 13 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a shut contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, because the first prints must absorb two Hormuz vessel strikes, Iranian attribution of one of them, Houthi fire into Saudi territory and Monday's Salalah diplomacy simultaneously in thin liquidity. Tail then decays to 19 by 03:00 UTC on the assumption of orderly two-sided price discovery, and the published danger window is deliberately limited to 22:00 UTC Sunday through 03:00 UTC Monday rather than the whole Monday session. Stress stays in the high band in every slot, between 65 and 71, and leads Tail throughout because a likely Fed hike, oil above $100, a 10-year near 5 per cent and an active regional conflict describe a difficult environment rather than a path that denies mean reversion. Monday's later slots shift toward positioning into Wednesday's FOMC.
